thread:
Priya Nair: quick sync — we need to pick a default ownership model for service-account tokens in Console before the quota/telemetry rollout. Customers are hitting weird billing attribution when an SA is used across multiple projects. do we treat tokens as project-scoped by default or allow floating (user-owned) tokens?
Alex Kim: my vote: project-scoped by default. simplest for billing & quotas: token -> project mapping = canonical. avoids surprises. :+1:
Jordan Lee: project-scoped helps metering, but we also need a clear exchange path for cross-project workflows. what about this hybrid: token has an origin_project claim (immutable) + current_project claim (changes on exchange). attribution defaults to origin_project unless overridden by explicit exchange header.
Priya Nair: sketch of Jordan's idea looks promising. need to nail telemetry keys we emit so billing/console can show a single source of truth.
Maya (design): UX note — if origin != current, Console should show a small banner "token used in project X via exchange from Y" not a full migration flow. keep it readable.
Alex Kim: implementation concerns: keeping "current_project" mutable means we need atomic updates when tokens are exchanged. could be done at auth-proxy level (no DB write) by issuing ephemeral impersonation tokens with claims.
Jordan Lee: exact example of the exchange flow I was thinking of:

```http
POST /v1/token/exchange
Authorization: Bearer SA_TOKEN
Accept: application/json
{
  "target_project": "proj-123",
  "purpose": "background-reindex"
}
```

Response issues a short-lived impersonation JWT with claims: origin_project=proj-999, current_project=proj-123, actor=sa:svc-42, exchange_path=[sa->proxy->service].
Priya Nair: good. for telemetry we should emit: token.id, origin_project, current_project, actor, exchange_reason, exchange_tier, and route (hosted/dedicated/private). that way we can compute charges either by origin or by current depending on UI filters.
SRE-Bot: suggestion: event schema proposal: `auth.exchange` with fields ["token_id","origin_project","current_project","actor","exchange_duration","route","node_id","latency_ms"]. keep event size small.
Alex Kim: concern: billing systems may want deterministic attribution. toggling between origin/current could cause disputes. propose default behavior = charge origin_project, with explicit flag in exchange to opt-in to charge current_project. make opt-in logged/auditable.
Maya (design): show "charged to" prominently in the exchange modal. if opting to charge current project require a 2nd confirm click and show cost estimate.
Jordan Lee: technical hitch: some legacy internal jobs expect SA to be project movable. forcing origin-charge may break them. migration idea: detect tokens already used cross-project historically and mark them as "legacy-floating" and keep old behavior, but new tokens get origin_project lock.
Priya Nair: rollout plan draft: 1) emit `auth.exchange` events for 2 weeks in all envs (no billing changes) 2) console additions: display origin/current + charge hint 3) opt-in flag for exchange requests (controller-level) 4) default billing = origin_project for 30 days canary 5) then make origin lock mandatory for new tokens and offer a migration tool for legacy-floating tokens.
Alex Kim: +1. add a telemetry-driven gate: if >95% of exchanges in canary are opt-in-to-current, reconsider.
Jordan Lee: also add an auditing endpoint so security teams can query all tokens that were exchanged into a project in a window.
Priya Nair: action items: Alex to draft opt-in flag + API shape, Jordan to draft token claim format and proxy flow, Maya to mock console banners/confirm modal, SRE-Bot to propose event schema and retention. I'll schedule a 30-min call Thurs to review.
Maya (design): tiny UX ask — include a tooltip on token listing that says "origin project locks new tokens to this project; existing legacy tokens may behave differently".
Alex Kim: one more engineering note: keep Authorization header unchanged for downstream services when using impersonation; prefer a downstream-friendly `X-Forwarded-Actor` header rather than rewriting bearer tokens. less chance of breaking integrations.
Jordan Lee: agreed. implement exchange to return short-lived JWT for internal infra use, and set `X-Forwarded-Actor`. we'll also add a small compatibility shim at auth-proxy for services that expect bearer token.
Priya Nair: thanks all — I'll post the draft rollout doc to the eng-platform repo and tag this thread. meeting invite incoming. :calendar:
